2609.40127.title: Learning Functional Subspaces for Neural Network Compression
2609.40127.paper_summary: Modern transformers pair impressive capabilities with substantial memory and compute demands. Low-rank weight factorization reduces both while keeping the matrices dense, and thus efficient on standard hardware. Existing methods, however, choose the subspace to remove from each weight matrix with local closed-form criteria: activation energy, layer-wise reconstruction error, or a quadratic approximation of the loss. These criteria ignore how errors propagate through the network, so at high compression the errors compound with depth and performance collapses. We introduce Learnable Subspace Projections (LSP), which instead learns the subspaces to discard end-to-end. Each linear layer, or tied group of layers that read the same activations, is assigned an orthogonal projector. All projectors are optimized jointly against a global objective--the KL divergence to the dense model's output distribution or the model's original training loss--while the pretrained weights remain frozen. Projectors are initialized from a whitened SVD truncation, and ranks are allocated by the output KL each projector induces per parameter saved. After training, the projectors merge into standard low-rank factors, with each tied group sharing one factor. In attention, this also lets the model cache one narrow latent in place of full keys and values. Across LLMs (OPT-125M/1.3B, Qwen3-4B, Llama-2-7B) and ViT-B/16, LSP outperforms baselines, and its advantage widens as compression increases. At -70% compression, LSP brings Llama-2-7B to 10.9 WikiText-2 perplexity and 42.2% mean zero-shot accuracy, versus 13.3 and 36.0% for the strongest baseline. The factorized model decodes up to 1.6x faster than the dense model at small batch sizes, and aching the shared latent shrinks the combined memory of weights and KV cache by 13.5x at a 128k-token context, versus at most 6.5x for untied baseline factorizations.
2609.40127.paper_summary_zh: 現代Transformer結合了令人印象深刻的能力與可觀的記憶和計算需求。低秩權重因式分解在保持矩陣密集的同時減少了這兩者，因此在標準硬體上效率高。然而，現有的方法選擇從每個權重矩陣中去除的子空間，使用局部閉合形式的標準：激活能量、層級重建誤差或損失的二次近似。這些標準忽略了誤差在網絡中的傳播，因此在高壓縮下，誤差隨著深度累積，性能崩潰。我們引入了可學習子空間投影（LSP），它學習要丟棄的子空間，從端到端進行。每個線性層或讀取相同激活的綁定層組被分配一個正交投影器。所有投影器都是針對一個全局目標共同優化的——即密集模型的輸出分佈或模型的原始訓練損失的KL散度，同時預訓練的權重保持不變。投影器從白化的SVD截斷初始化，並根據每個投影器每個保存的參數所引起的輸出KL分配秩。在訓練後，投影器合併成標準的低秩因子，每個綁定組共享一個因子。在注意力中，這也使模型能夠在不使用完整鍵和值的情況下緩存一個狹窄的潛在表示。在大型語言模型（OPT-125M/1.3B、Qwen3-4B、Llama-2-7B）和ViT-B/16中，LSP超越基準，其優勢隨著壓縮的增加而擴大。在-70%的壓縮下，LSP將Llama-2-7B的WikiText-2困惑度降低到10.9，零-shot平均準確率為42.2%，而最強基準則為13.3和36.0%。在小批量大小下，因式分解模型的解碼速度比密集模型快最多1.6倍，並且共享潛在表示使得權重和KV緩存的總記憶在128k-token上下文中縮小了13.5倍，而未綁定基準因式分解最多僅縮小6.5倍。
